MBG 101.name: Biology I
MBG 101.description: Molecules of life, central dogma (from DNA to protein), manipulation and analysis of nucleic acids and proteins. An introduction to genetics, immunology, development and cancer.

MBG 102.name: Biology II
MBG 102.description: Introduction to cell division and differentiation introduction to the molecular biology methods, recombinant DNA technology, biotechnology. (Laboratory work is obligatory)

MBG 105.name: Principles of Biology
MBG 105.description: This course is for students from the Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics Departments. Molecules of life, organization of the cell, chromosomes and cell division, patterns of inheritance, evolution, recombinant DNA technology, genetic diseases.

MBG 110.name: Introduction to Modern Biology
MBG 110.description: This course introduces students to important topics of biology such as molecules of life, organization of the cell, chromosomes and cell division, genetics, molecular genetics, recombinant DNA technology, genetic diseases, evolution, animal development, biotechnology and recent scientific advancements.

MBG 209.name: Principles of Genetics
MBG 209.description: Transmission genetics, gene and chromosomal mutations, linkage and mapping, molecular genetic applications, population and quantitative genetics, molecular evolution, model organism genomics and bioinformatics.

MBG 210.name: Genetics
MBG 210.description: Mendelian genetics, chromosome theory of inheritance, linkage, genetic mapping in eukaryotes and prokaryotes, chromosomal mutations, gene mutations, molecular genetics, population genetics, quantitative genetics, molecular evolution.

MBG 222.name: Fundamentals of Molecular Genetics
MBG 222.description: Molecular biology of gene regulation, fundamentals of DNA repair and recombination, detailed analysis of transposition and retroposition in eukaryotes, molecular mechanisms of eukaryotic and prokaryotic protein synthesis.

MBG 223.name: Molecular Genetics
MBG 223.description: Mechanism of protein synthesis, usage of the genetic code, protein localization, the structure of genetic material, regulation of transcription, recombination, repair, and transposition in bacteria, an introduction to gene rearrangements. (Laboratory work is obligatory )

MBG 230.name: Experimental Approaches in Molecular and Cellular Biology
MBG 230.description: This course introduce a substantial theoretical basis to understand key experimental techniques used in modern molecular biology research; focusing on the techniques and concepts that involve genetic engineering; restriction enzymes, cloning DNA plasmid constructs and the analysis of DNA/RNA samples, creating and screening a library, probe labeling and hybridization, PCR, q-RT-PCR, DNA sequencing techniques, manipulating gene expression in prokaryotes, heterologous protein production in eukaryotes, cell growth and cytotoxicity assays, Cell adhesion, invasion, motility, apoptosis assays, molecular diagnostics, protein therapeutics, nucleic acids as therapeutics, transgenic animals. It provides to students with a thorough understanding of the physical-chemical and biological principles underlying the most basic techniques and procedures used in molecular biology. Examples will be given on learning how to understand and interpret results generated through these methods.

MBG 291.name: Summer Practice I
MBG 291.description: A project on a special topic in an area of biology to be carried out by the student under the supervision of a faculty member, at the department or another institution. This course provides students with an internship experience allowing the application of lab techniques in broad areas of molecular biology genetics and the practicing of their skills in scientific environments. Students will work full-time at an academic setting, research institute or an industrial site for a minimum of 20 working days.

MBG 301.name: Molecular Biology of the Cell I
MBG 301.description: This course aims an in-depth understanding of cell signaling. We start by studying the signal/receptor families individually, and move on to a synthesis by studying examples from developmental biology and cancer. Selected original articles that from the foundations and principles of cell signaling are analyzed and criticized thoroughly as part of the coursework.

MBG 302.name: Molecular Biology of the Cell II
MBG 302.description: Germ cells and fertilization, early embryonic development, stem cells, generation and maintenance of differentiated cells, immune cells, cancer cells, specialized techniques in cell biology, light and fluorescent microscopy, flow cytometry, techniques used for cell proliferation and apoptosis studies. (Laboratory work is obligatory).

MBG 311.name: Biochemistry I
MBG 311.description: Introductory biochemistry, bioenergetics, protein structure, protein purification and characterization, enzymatic activity, kinetics, allostery, vitamins and coenzymes.

MBG 312.name: Biochemistry II
MBG 312.description: Introduction to intermediary metabolism, polysaccharides, energy storage, lipids and membrane structure nucleic acid structure and nucleotide metabolism.

MBG 316.name: Physiology
MBG 316.description: Homeostatic and biological control mechanisms in major body systems, including skeletal system, muscle system, nervous system, circulatory system, respiratory system, digestive system, excretory system, reproductive system and immune system.

MBG 324.name: Molecular Biology of the Gene
MBG 324.description: Molecular biology of eukaryotes including genome organization and chromosome structure, chromatin structure, eukaryotic transcription, promoters and enhancers, eukaryotic transcription regulation. Epigenetics effect on gene expression, RNA splicing and processing, regulatory RNAs. (Laboratory work is obligatory)

MBG 326.name: Introduction to Bioinformatics
MBG 326.description: Introduction to Bioinformatics: Computer use in molecular biology, access to online databases, sequence alignment, phylogenetics, RNA expression analysis, GWAS statistics, gene networks.

MBG 338.name: Microbiology
MBG 338.description: Structure, growth and physiology of microorganisms, classification of bacteria, diverse activities of bacteria, viruses, microbial pathogenicity, exploitation of microorganisms by man.

MBG 391.name: Summer Practice II
MBG 391.description: A project on a special topic in an area of biology to be carried out by the student under the supervision of a faculty member, at the department or another institution.

MBG 416.name: Science and Ethics
MBG 416.description: Scientific concepts, history of science, the birth of modern science, science and society, ethics of science.

MBG 418.name: Genomics
MBG 418.description: High throughput methods for the analysis of DNA and RNA. Repetitive sequences, comparative genomics, transcriptomics, metagenomics, epigenomics, evolutionary genomics, systems biology.

MBG 452.name: Practical Biology
MBG 452.description: This course is for students from faculty of Education. Practical techniques for the biology laboratory, biological experiments, and problem solving in biology. The course involves one hour of discussion and four hours of laboratory work per week. The students carry out practical projects.

MBG 466.name: Introduction to Cellular and Molecular Biology of the Brain
MBG 466.description: Fundamentals of development, structure, cellular biology of the nervous system. Synaptic and systems-level communication. Brain function in health and diseases.

MBG 470.name: Immunology
MBG 470.description: This course will provide students with a fundamental understanding of immunobiology. Topics will include basic concepts in immunology, innate and adaptive immunity, regulation of immune system, immune system in health and disease, and manipulation of the immune response.

MBG 472.name: Introduction to Stem Cells
MBG 472.description: Basic biology of embryonic, adult and cancer stem cells. Molecular mechanisms of self-renewal, differentiation and plasticity. Reproductive and therapeutic cloning. Epigenetic changes associated with stem cells. Use of stem cells in cell based therapies and its ethical considerations.

MBG 473.name: Biomolecules, Biomaterials and Bioprocesses
MBG 473.description: Utilization of biological macromolecules as a biomaterial, principles applied to harness these biological complex molecules in biology, medicine and pharmaceutical biotechnology discussion of the selected cutting edge research papers.

MBG 474.name: Introduction to Computational Biology
MBG 474.description: Introduction to computational Biology: Methods and exercises in phylogenetics, microarray data analysis, systems biology.

MBG 481.name: Protein Chemistry
MBG 481.description: Introduction to protein structure and the principles of protein structure with examples of key proteins. Specific examples of proteins to show how they fulfill a wide range of biological functions. In silico approaches to determining and predicting protein structure.

MBG 483.name: Developmental Biology
MBG 483.description: Embryonic development of Drosophila, zebrafish, chick, xenopus and mouse. Manipulating gene expression during development. Analyzing gene function during development. Analyzing cell fate and tissue interactions in embryos.

MBG 485.name: DNA Damage and Repair Mechanisms
MBG 485.description: Types of DNA damage and the cellular response to it. DNA repair mechanisms: direct reversal of repair, base-excision, nucleotide-excision, mis-match repair, homologous recombination repair, non-homologous end joining.

MBG 487.name: Special Techniques in Molecular Genetics
MBG 487.description: Principles of specific methods used in the molecular genetics, laboratory tools for molecular genetic applications, restriction enzymes, cloning vectors, gene Analysis methods, DNA cloning, gene libraries and library screening, PCR and other applications, expression of cloned genes in cultured cells, isolation and characterization of gene transcripts, RNA analysis, microarray analysis, proteomics , RNA world and RNA knockdown strategies, gene manipulations in animals, gene and cellular therapies. Discussions of selected research papers. (No lab session.)

MBG 488.name: Introduction to Human Genetics
MBG 488.description: Principles of human genetics, patterns of single gene inheritance, human molecular genetics, the human gene map, cytogenetics, the molecular and biochemical basis of genetic disease, genetic counseling, prenatal diagnosis.

MBG 489.name: Genetics and Biology of Cancer
MBG 489.description: Genetic changes in cancer, phenotype of cancer cells, oncogenes, tumor suppressor genes, hereditary cancers, cell cycle, apoptosis, senescence, DNA repair and cancer, multicellular interactions in cancer.

MBG 491.name: Senior Project I
MBG 491.description: A project on a specific topic in an area of molecular biology or genetics to be carried out by the student under the supervision of a faculty member.

MBG 492.name: Senior Project with Thesis
MBG 492.description: A project focusing on a specific topic in molecular biology or genetics, undertaken by the student under the guidance of a faculty member. This project will include extensive independent research and culminate in a formal written thesis, which the student will defend in an oral presentation.

MBG 502.name: Advanced Cellular Biology
MBG 502.description: Cell structure and function, the cytoskeleton, intracellular compartments, vesicular trafficking, the cell-division cycle, cell junctions, cell adhesion, extracellular matrix and development.

MBG 503.name: Advanced Molecular Biology
MBG 503.description: Chromosomal DNA and its packaging, higher-order organization of chromosomes, replication, recombination, eukaryotic transcription regulation, DNA repair, RNA modifications and RNA world, alternative splicing, epigenetics. Discussions of selected research papers.

MBG 505.name: Advanced Molecular Genetics
MBG 505.description: Organization of the genome, Mendelian and non-Mendelian inheritance, mitochondrial genome, multigene families and repetitive DNA, polymorphism and polymorphic markers, genetic mapping, physical mapping, models of studying gene structure and function.

MBG 509.name: Special Topics in Molecular Biology I
MBG 509.description: Current topics in molecular biology, comprehensive reading, critical evaluations of scientific references, seminar presentations and class participation.

MBG 510.name: Special Topics in Molecular Biology II
MBG 510.description: Current topics in molecular biology, comprehensive reading, critical evaluations of scientific references, seminar presentations and class participation.

MBG 513.name: Bioinformatics
MBG 513.description: Commonly used databases in molecular biology, genetics and related fields, homology search for genes and proteins, primer design, microarray analysis, Next Generation Sequencing data analysis, systems biology and gene/protein networks.

MBG 514.name: Stem Cell Biology
MBG 514.description: The aim of the course is to integrate organismal, cellular, genetic and molecular approaches to the study of stem cell biology. We will discuss a diversity of mechanisms, ranging from 3D culture to therapeutic approach of stem cells. Molecular mechanisms of self-renewal, differentiation and plasticity of the stem cells will be covered.

MBG 516.name: Biomolecules, Biomaterials and Bioprocesses
MBG 516.description: Basic biomolecules (from simple molecules such as aminoacids to macro molecules such as proteins and DNA) and principles of biology from material science perspective. This course must be a core course given very early in the curriculum.

MBG 523.name: Recent Developments in Molecular Biology
MBG 523.description: Latest developments and emerging issues in molecular biology including nucleosome and chromatin structure, RNA polymerase II Holoenzyme and its roles, transcription and regulation, chromatin modifying and remodeling complexes, tissue specific gene expression, DNA replication, repair and recombination, cell cycle and regulation. Discussion on the selected articles.

MBG 599.name: Master's Thesis
MBG 599.description: A research-based thesis course offers students the opportunity to independently carry out a complete scientific work process, including the understanding of theoretical background, hypothesis generation, collection and analysis of data, and interpretation and presentation of results with the supervision of the thesis supervisor. Master the methods necessary to carry out the relevant research project connected to the thesis. Communicate one's own research results in a scientifically correct fashion, both in written and oral contexts. To complete a written thesis and an oral defense presenting the research findings with intellectual analysis are necessary for the assessment of the eligibility of graduation by the end of the study.

MBG 601.name: Human Genetics
MBG 601.description: Molecular genetics of human diseases, chromosomal abnormalities, biochemical genetics, genetic basis of cancer, genome projects, molecular medicine, genetic counseling, DNA based diagnostics, population genetics.

MBG 602.name: Molecular and Cellular Immunology
MBG 602.description: This course will provide students with a fundamental understanding of immunobiology. Topics will include basic concepts in immunology, innate and adaptive immunity, regulation of immune system, immune system in health and disease, and manipulation of the immune response.

MBG 603.name: Molecular Bases of Cancer
MBG 603.description: Cancer as a multi gene disease, oncogenes, tumor suppressor genes, mutator genes, gene therapy of cancer, germ-line and somatic mutations and cancer, genes involved in abnormal proliferation and metastatic behavior of cancer cells, immune response to cancer, familial cancers, virus-induced cancers.

MBG 612.name: Special Topics in Genetics I
MBG 612.description: Current topics in molecular genetics, comprehensive reading, critical evaluation of scientific literatures seminar presentations and class participation.

MBG 613.name: Special Topics in Genetics II
MBG 613.description: Current topics in molecular genetics, comprehensive reading, critical evaluation of scientific literatures seminar presentations and class participation.

MBG 615.name: Recent Advances in Molecular Biology
MBG 615.description: Latest developments and emerging issues on molecular biology including cancer, cell-cell interactions, extra- cellular matrix, signal transduction, chromatin formation. Discussions on recent techniques with active student participation.

MBG 616.name: Experimental Molecular Biology and Genetics I
MBG 616.description: An introduction to basic molecular biology and genetics techniques. The student spends a half semester with one of the research groups and participates in some aspects of the research being pursued by the faculty member.

MBG 617.name: Experimental Molecular Biology and Genetics II
MBG 617.description: An introduction to advanced molecular biology and genetics techniques. The student spends a half semester with one of the research groups and participates in some aspects of the research being pursued by the faculty member.

MBG 623.name: Seminars in Molecular Genetics I
MBG 623.description: The course will be based on class presentations and discussions of novel concepts in Molecular Genetics. Articles selected by the staff will be introduced and discussed with the students in the form of paper presentations and seminars. Students will be encourage to carry out a critical analysis of novel as well as milestone "classical" articles in the field of Molecular Genetics.

MBG 624.name: Seminars in Molecular Genetics II
MBG 624.description: The course will be based on class presentations and discussions of novel concepts in Molecular Genetics. Articles selected by the staff will be introduced and discussed with the students in the form of paper presentations and seminars. Students will be encourage to carry out a critical analysis of novel as well as milestone "classical" articles in the field of Molecular Genetics.

MBG 699.name: Ph.D. Dissertation
MBG 699.description: A research-based thesis course offers students the opportunity to independently carry out a complete scientific work process, including the understanding of theoretical background, hypothesis generation, collection and analysis of data, and interpretation and presentation of results with the supervision of the thesis supervisor. The students successfully complete the qualifying examination and proposal assessment can carry out to evaluate and apply relevant theory, methods and analytic approaches within the field of research. To complete a written thesis and an oral defense presenting the research findings with intellectual analysis are necessary for the assessment of the eligibility of graduation by the end of the study.
